correctness.rationale: For \(S=z_1^2+z_2^2\), \(r=|z_3|\), the estimates \(|S|\le1-r^2\) and \((1-r^2)^m+\varepsilon r^2\le1-(1-\varepsilon)r^2\) exclude every interior zero and every boundary zero with \(r>0\). Equality in the triangle inequality gives exactly \(m\) phase-rotated real circles, distinct modulo \(\pi\). Over \(\mathbb C[z_1,z_2]\), the prime \(q=1-S\) is irreducible via \(u=z_1+iz_2\), \(v=z_1-iz_2\), and \(1-S^m\) has prime-factor valuation exactly one because the complementary sum is \(m\bmod q\). Eisenstein in \(z_3\) gives irreducibility. Nonzero gradient gives smoothness; Hermitian tangency is explicit; each circle is a fiber of an orthogonal-complex-structure Hopf fibration of the equatorial \(S^3\), so all pairs link with absolute number one. No numerical test or unproved lemma is substituted for the infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: This is a natural topology-versus-irreducibility boundary for holomorphic zero avoidance: the standard one-variable lifted \(m\)-circle construction factors for \(m>1\), while the new globally stable perturbation is irreducible without deleting or moving any boundary component. It proves an unbounded connected-component invariant within fixed dimension and irreducible defining polynomials and simultaneously gives a complete Hopf-link pattern; these are genuine geometric features not supplied by finite stratification or a one-component quadratic model. It is not a routine degree-specific example, numerical cutoff, or merely renamed known formula.
